description: This minor course gives fundamental concepts of control system design, performance analysis of systems, modeling errors, sensitivity, robustness, feedback control design, predictive controllers and anti-wind-up schemes.

syllabus.title: System Models
syllabus.body: Review of system models, model simplifications and associated modeling errors, control-ratio modeling, discrete time and hybrid models, canonical decomposition.

syllabus.title: Stability and Performance
syllabus.body: Stability and performance specifications, limits of performance, modeling errors, constraints on sensitivity, complementary sensitivity, robustness.

syllabus.title: Controller Design
syllabus.body: Design of linear state feedback, compensating delays, Smith predictors, predictive controllers, internal model control.

syllabus.title: Recent Trends
syllabus.body: Recent trends in control system design, control design based on identification of complex systems, integrator wind up and anti-wind up schemes, PID synthesis using the affine parameterization, design exercises and case studies.

outcomes: Develop mathematical models and understand the mathematical relationships between the sensitivity functions.
Perform stability analysis and study the performance of closed-loop systems.
Design a feedback controller and follow a specific design procedure.
Develop predictive controllers and identification of complex systems.
textbooks: G. C. Goodwin, S. F. Graebe and M. E. Salgado, Control System Design, Prentice Hall of India, 2001.
B. Friedland, Advanced Control System Design, Prentice Hall Int. Inc., NY, 1966.
John J. D'Azzo and Constantine H. Houpis, Linear Control System Analysis and Design: Conventional and Modern, McGraw-Hill, 4th Edition, 1995.
referenceBooks: Raymond T. Stefani, Bahram Shahian, Clement J. Savant and Gene H. Hostetter, Design of Feedback Control Systems, Oxford University Press, 4th Edition, 2001.
